transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-09-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Blueleaf - Head of ML), Daniel O'Neill (Blueleaf - Platform), Sara Thompson (Blueleaf - SRE)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync to review recent reliability regressions — intermittent 502/5xx spikes and client-observed timeouts. Discussed telemetry gaps, KV cache cold-start effects, rate-limit windows, and an initial mitigation plan (dedicated routing for a subset of traffic + retry/backoff tuning). Agreed on follow-ups: perf sheet, reproducer tests, 10% dedicated routing toggle, and a deep dive on KV cache warming.

Topics covered:
- 5xx patterns and correlation with sequence length and tokenization
- Client retry behavior and budgeting
- KV cache warmup and hot-shard effects
- Rate-limit bursts vs sustained throughput
- Security/compliance note: SOC2 questions and KMS integration for private pilots

Action items (captured verbally in call):
- See action_items list in metadata

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. short agenda, quick recap of last week's tests, then we want to walk through the 5xx traces you attached, and then outline the mitigation plan.
[00:28] Priya (Blueleaf): thanks avery. yeah we've seen a mix of 502 and 504s during peak windows, and some client timeouts when sequence lengths go above 1,200 tokens. it's intermittent and not obviously traffic-volume correlated.
[00:45] Mateo (Redwood SE): ok, that's helpful. just to confirm — are the 502s coming with any consistent error message or are they generic upstream 5xxs? the traces you uploaded had a few different traces.
[01:05] Sara (Blueleaf SRE): most are generic "upstream response error" but in one batch it looked like the worker OOM in the logs, though that might be a red herring because it didn't align with GPU memory metrics. the timing though is suspicious — many around ~23:10 UTC.
[01:28] Daniel (Blueleaf): we capture request ids in our proxy, so we can match them. i've put some example request ids in the ticket, we can hand those over.
[01:40] Avery: perfect. Mateo, can you share the quick checklist for causes?
[01:48] Mateo: yeah so from the runtime side, top suspects: (1) KV cache cold miss + long compile path, (2) adaptive batching edge-case when small short requests interleave with long ones, (3) transient rate-window enforcement causing queue drops, and (4) occasional model variant fallback that wasn't warm. also quantization path differences sometimes expose model-level crashes in older kernels.
[02:15] Priya: kv cache — do you mean the prefix cache? we rely on a lot of repeated prompts so if cache isn't sticky that could explain the spike.
[02:26] Mateo: exactly, prefix / KV cache. when a pod restarts or a worker is cold, the kv cache is empty and the first few requests pay extra work; if this lines up with retry storms on the client we can amplify the problem.
[02:40] Sara: we're also seeing an uptick in 429s before the 502s sometimes. so i'm wondering if the client is retrying aggressively causing thundering herd.
[02:52] Avery: that's classic. i want to be explicit about the retry budget: client should back off with jitter and cap retries to X for production — we'll propose exact numbers.
[03:05] Daniel: what about dedicated vs hosted? we were thinking about moving a small slice to dedicated capacity for the pilot to reduce noisy neighbor issues.
[03:16] Mateo: that's a good experiment. dedicated pool reduces cross-tenant variance but you still need to handle KV cache warmup and cold-starts on scale events. the benefit is more predictable tail latencies.
[03:30] Priya: and from compliance side, dedicated plus VPC matters — but we also need KMS integration so logs and payloads are encrypted to our key.
[03:42] Avery: noted. ksm — KMS integration? we do support customer-managed keys for Private, for Dedicated we have an option via partner KMS — we'll pull in the security doc after the call.
[03:58] Mateo: going back to the traces — i pulled the stack for a couple of the sample req ids. here's the pattern i saw: a quick sequence where the request enters, the batcher holds for 25ms, then a fallback attempted to a quantized variant after kernel failure, the fallback path then timed out at model runtime and we returned 502. it's not purely network.
[04:28] Priya: does that mean kernel selection could be flaky?
[04:32] Mateo: in practice it's deterministic but under partial resource pressure and mixed sequence lengths we saw a path where our kernel probe hit an unsupported op and we triggered fallback. that fallback path hasn't been as well exercised in your workload.
[04:48] Sara: how do we validate that? can we run a synthetic with your exact model binary and our prompt set?
[04:55] Avery: yes, we can. Mateo, do we have a reproducer?
[05:00] Mateo: i can build a targeted load test — mix of short 50-token and long 1,500-token prompts, with retries per client spec. if we see the same kernel fallback pattern, we'll try to isolate which op triggers the fallback.
[05:18] Daniel: also, our client currently retries on 5xx with exponential backoff but no jitter, and max 5 retries. we can change that.
[05:29] Avery: please change that to capped 3 retries with full jitter and an initial base of 200ms — we'll propose exact numbers in writing. also add idempotency token handling for non-idempotent generation calls.
[05:45] Priya: any quick mitigations we can apply today while Mateo runs tests?
[05:50] Mateo: short-term: (1) reduce client retries to avoid retry storms, (2) route 10% of traffic to a dedicated pilot pool to see if noisy neighbors are a factor, (3) instrument a KV cache heat-up metric and emit a flag when miss rate > threshold.
[06:10] Sara: how do we route 10%? via header or routing rule?
[06:15] Avery: we can do a routing rule on customer id or header, we'll share the exact curl and curl example.
[06:22] Daniel: ok we'll do that tomorrow.
[06:25] Mateo: one more observation — some of the 504/timeouts align with long tail disk IO on the node that hosts the model partition. if you have on-prem storage or bursty NFS this could show up. Blueleaf is cloud-only though right?
[06:42] Priya: yes cloud only but we do have some attached volume backups running at night. could be coincident.
[06:48] Avery: sounds like we need both infra and runtime checks. Mateo will run reproducer, Blueleaf will flip routing and adjust retries, and Avery will share perf sheet and the security doc.
[07:00] Sara: on the security/compliance item — we need SOC2 artifact showing data segregation for dedicated pool and the KMS integration guide.
[07:08] Avery: i'll send SOC2 extract and a short KMS integration note after.
[07:12] Daniel: what's the expected uplift or change we hope to see when moving 10% of traffic to dedicated?
[07:19] Mateo: ideally you'd see narrower p95/p99 bands and fewer tail 5xxs if noisy neighbors are the root cause. if it's KV warmup, dedicated won't eliminate the cold-start complexity but will make it easier to instrument.
[07:33] Priya: i'm concerned about the model fallback — if a kernel mismatch triggers fallback to a quantized variant, that might change output quality. we need quality regression checks too.
[07:44] Avery: good point. we'll tie the rollout to a small eval harness — run the top 200 prompts and compare logits or classification outputs. if quality drops beyond threshold we'll rollback.
[07:57] Mateo: technical note: we'll also add a small delay for the first few requests to let the KV cache warm, and pre-warm cache with a replay of recent sessions. that's part of the follow-up plan.
[08:10] Priya: can you pre-warm from our dataset? there's PII considerations.
[08:16] Avery: we can do a replay on customer-controlled data in a private tenant if you give us brief access, or you can run the pre-warm script in your environment. we'll provide both options.
[08:29] Daniel: final question on observability — what new metrics should we be tracking?
[08:33] Mateo: kv_cache_miss_rate, kernel_fallback_count, batch_hold_ms distribution, per-worker gpu_mem_faults, and queue_drop_rate. also correlate with client retry counters.
[08:45] Sara: please include log snippets with request ids so we can stitch across systems.
[08:49] Avery: we'll include that in the perf spreadsheet.
[09:00] Priya: ok i think we have alignment. quick recap?
[09:04] Avery: recap: (1) blueleaf to route 10% to dedicated, (2) blueleaf to reduce client retries and add jitter, (3) Mateo to run reproducer and surface kernel fallback traces, (4) Avery to send perf sheet + security doc. follow-up deep dive scheduled.
[09:22] Daniel: sounds good. one minor ask — can you include a quick note on expected cost delta for 10% dedicated?
[09:29] Avery: yes i'll include an estimated cost delta in the email.
[09:33] Priya: thanks everyone.
[09:35] Avery: thanks all, we'll sync next week or earlier if Mateo finds the reproducer.
[09:40] (call ends)
